The Liang Province page: 'proposals to abandon Liang Province', rebellion 'quelled in 118'. The Lanzhou circle is a stand-in for Longxi (not placed on either page); the extent beyond Hanyang and Longxi is not given.

ledger.note: 107: the Qiang rise. 'In 107 CE, the Xianlian Qiang rebelled against Han authority' (Liang Province page); they 'elected a Xianlian chieftain, Dianlian as their leader' and after beating the Han army at Hanyang 'Dianlian proclaimed himself emperor' (Qiang page, no year for the title).

region.text: Hanyang Commandery, where the Han army was defeated

ledger.note: 107: the war with the Han opens. 'the Han court sent Deng Zhi and Ren Shang against them'; the Han army was beaten at Hanyang Commandery. The Qiang page gives no month; the protectorate in the Tarim was abandoned the same year.
109: Longxi falls. 'In 109 CE, he conquered Longxi'; in 110 Dianlian killed the Administrator of Hanzhong (a raid beyond the held ground).

ledger.note: 118: the First Great Qiang Rebellion is over. 'After heavy fighting, and proposals to abandon Liang Province, this First Great Qiang Rebellion was quelled in 118'; the Qiang page has Dianlian dead in 112, Lianchang's headquarters attacked in 116 and Lianchang 'assassinated the next year, and forces under Ren Shang ended the Qiang raids'.

wars.outcome: The Qiang beat the Han at Hanyang, took Longxi in 109 and raided Hanzhong in 110; Dianlian died in 112, Lianchang was attacked in 116 and killed in 117; the revolt was quelled in 118.

notes:
Qiang rebels of Dianlian and Lianchang, 107-118 (rebel). 2 pages opened (Qiang (historical people), Liang Province); no Cliopatria row; the Han Dynasty dossier (ea-02-c) carries a contest 107-118 with 'qiang'.
Unsettled: (1) the Qiang page's end (117, Lianchang killed 'the next year' after 116) against the Liang Province page's 118: 118 used; (2) the Qiang page gives the year for Longxi (109) and Hanzhong (110) but none for the Hanyang victory or Dianlian's title; (3) the extent of the rebel-held ground is not on any page (Hexi and Guanzhong uprisings are on the Protectorate page ea-02-c cites, not opened here); (4) no capital is named; (5) the Xianlian's earlier and later revolts (167, the Dongqiang 167-169) are not in this dossier's life; the Shaodang chieftain Dianyu's 57 invasion of Jincheng is outside it too.
Counterparts: han-dynasty exists; 'qiang' is the slug ea-02-c and ea-02-d proposed.
